reasoning: Recent general-election polling for Michigan’s 2026 Senate race consistently shows a very tight contest, with a slight but non-uniform Republican edge when Abdul El-Sayed is the Democratic nominee and a roughly even race when Haley Stevens is tested. Across the last 45 days of statewide general-election polls, Republican Mike Rogers typically leads El-Sayed by around mid–single to low–double digits but runs roughly tied with or slightly behind Stevens, so the current general-election environment is best characterized as R+ a few points if El-Sayed is the nominee and roughly EVEN if Stevens is. Michigan’s statewide Cook Partisan Voting Index is EVEN, indicating a structurally balanced state where small shifts in opinion can decide the race.

sources.name: Glengariff Group / Michigan Education Association & Business Leaders for Michigan (reported by Breitbart, Jewish Insider)
sources.details: Glengariff Group statewide poll commissioned by the Michigan Education Association and Business Leaders for Michigan found Mike Rogers leading Abdul El-Sayed 49.0% to 38.7% among all voters (R+10.3) while Rogers trailed Haley Stevens 45.5% to 44.7% (D+0.8, effectively tied).

sources.name: Glengariff Group / Michigan Education Association & Business Leaders for Michigan (reported by Jewish Insider)
sources.details: Jewish Insider’s report on the same Glengariff statewide survey noted Haley Stevens leading Mike Rogers by 2 points (47% to 45%) among definite general-election voters while Abdul El-Sayed trailed Rogers by 7 points, underscoring a Republican advantage if El-Sayed is nominee but a toss-up if Stevens is.

sources.name: Mitchell Research (as summarized by media/poll-tracking report)
sources.details: A Mitchell Research poll of likely voters reported that Mike Rogers was tied with Abdul El-Sayed 45%–45% (EVEN) and led Haley Stevens 45%–41% (R+4) in hypothetical 2026 Senate matchups.

sources.name: EPIC-MRA (reported by The Hill)
sources.details: An EPIC-MRA poll described by The Hill found that 44% of respondents said they would vote for or consider voting for Haley Stevens and 42% said the same of Mike Rogers in a Michigan Senate test, implying a narrow Democratic-leaning but effectively toss-up race.

sources.name: EPIC-MRA (reported by The Blaze)
sources.details: Coverage of EPIC-MRA polling noted that one survey wave showed Rogers with a three-point lead over Abdul El-Sayed and essentially tied with or slightly trailing Haley Stevens, reinforcing a small GOP edge versus El-Sayed and a near-even race versus Stevens.

sources.name: Fox News Poll (Michigan Senate)
sources.details: A Fox News survey of Michigan registered voters found Mike Rogers leading Abdul El-Sayed 51% to 47% in a 2026 Senate general-election test, a 4-point Republican advantage within the poll’s margin of error.

sources.name: Emerson College Polling / WLNS / WOOD TV
sources.details: An Emerson College Polling/WLNS/WOOD TV survey of the Michigan Democratic Senate primary found Abdul El-Sayed leading Haley Stevens 54% to 39% (or 57%–41% including leaners), indicating El-Sayed as the likely Democratic nominee but providing only primary, not general-election, data.

sources.name: Multiple Democratic primary polls summarized by The New York Times
sources.details: A New York Times overview of Michigan Democratic Senate primary polling compiled several July surveys (Zenith Research, SoCal Strategies, Emerson, Tavern Research, Tulchin) all showing Abdul El-Sayed leading Haley Stevens by roughly 10–19 points, establishing him as primary frontrunner rather than measuring the general-election margin.

sources.name: WLNS / Emerson College Democratic primary coverage
sources.details: WLNS’s local writeup of the Emerson College Democratic primary poll reported El-Sayed ahead of Stevens 54% to 39% among likely primary voters, reflecting intraparty strength but not the statewide general electorate.

sources.name: EPIC-MRA/MIRS (reported by The Blaze)
sources.details: An EPIC-MRA/MIRS survey referenced in commentary indicated Rogers with a three-point lead over El-Sayed but slightly behind Stevens, reinforcing that general-election matchups are sensitive to which Democrat is nominated rather than providing a single fixed margin.

sources.name: Cook Political Report Partisan Voting Index (Michigan statewide)
sources.details: The Cook Political Report’s Partisan Voting Index lists Michigan’s statewide PVI as EVEN, meaning the state’s average presidential vote is in line with the national partisan balance, which serves as structural rather than race-specific data.
